description:
The same bug class bedrock-q67.21.17 removed from listings survives one layer up: a listed key whose version will not parse is silently discarded, so the caller reads a shorter history as fact.

- chunk_reader.ex:269 — latest_version/1 returns nil when no key parses, which callers read as 'no chunks exist'.
- snapshot.ex:149 — Stream.reject(&is_nil/1) drops entries whose version did not extract.

Both make a shard look OLDER or EMPTIER than it is. A corrupt key name, or one written in a future format this build does not understand, is indistinguishable from absence — which is precisely the conflation q67.21.17 eliminated at the listing boundary.

ChunkReader already refuses this elsewhere and states why: list_chunk_metadata/2 raises ChunkReader.ReadError on a header that will not decode 'to avoid silent replay gaps' (chunk_reader.ex:90), with an explicit :on_error option for callers that genuinely want tolerance. The key-parse path should follow the same convention rather than deciding silently on the caller's behalf.

Found by the PR #202 cold audit while sweeping for other instances; these were the only two in object_storage/, demux/ and materializer/.
title: [BUG] Unparseable object keys are silently dropped, making shards look older or emptier
